Syntax

The complete language, built-in functions, and every library. Also in the repository as SYNTAX.en.txt.

Nothing matches that search. Try a function name like len or a word like list.

Running and building

Run a script:

nrxlang run contoh_fitur.nrxl

Turn it into an .exe (needs gcc: bundled with the installer, or gcc on PATH; without gcc, build stops with a "you need gcc" message, and the script can still be run with run):

nrxlang build contoh_fitur.nrxl    -> contoh_fitur.exe
nrxlang build game.nrxl -o out\game.exe
  • The .exe stands alone: the .nrxl file (and every file it pulls in with im) is embedded, so the .nrxl files do not need to be shared.
  • Type errors are caught at build time, and no .exe is made.
  • Output and error messages of the .exe are exactly the same as running the script directly.
  • Math with int, double, and bool variables is much faster in the .exe (they become plain C variables). The syntax does not change.
  • lib nrx_window.h and ffi can be built too.
  • When nrxl is installed with the installer, gcc comes with it (the gcc folder next to nrxlang.exe), so there is no need to install gcc yourself.

After changing any .c file, rebuild (build.bat):

build

The output goes to dist\: nrxlang.exe, libnrxrt.a (runtime for built programs), and include\ (headers for the generated C code). nrxlang build looks for libnrxrt.a and include\ in the same folder as nrxlang.exe.

Files a script reads (readFile, playSound, newImage, ...) are looked up from the folder the command runs in, not the script's folder. The exception is im: files for im are looked up from the script's folder.

Basics

# comment         Comment until the end of the line. # inside quotes is
                  not a comment.
indentation       Spaces/tabs at the start of a line decide what belongs
                  to a block (if, loop, for, func, try, options).
one line          A statement must fit on one line.

Value kinds:

number    5   -3  (int)      2.5   5.0   1e3  (double)
text      "Hello"
bool      true   false
list      [1, 2, 3]   ["apple", "orange"]   (all items one kind)
map       {"Budi": 20, "Sari": 21}   (all values one kind)
array     array(1000)   array([1, 2.5])  (a row of decimal numbers, see below)
type      Player("Budi", 100)            (see section 8)

Escapes inside text:

\n    new line
\t    tab
\r    back to the start of the line (to overwrite, e.g. progress)
\"    quote
\\    backslash

Write file paths with / (for example "C:/data/a.txt"), because \n in "C:\new" is read as a new line.

Error message language:

errlang = en                 # errors in English
errlang = id                 # errors in Indonesian
  • Without errlang, the language follows Windows: Indonesian Windows gets Indonesian errors, any other language gets English.
  • errlang is only allowed in the main file, at the far left. It applies to the whole program, including files pulled in with im.
  • Every error has the same code in every language, for example: error E0003 in game.nrxl:5: variable skor has not been created error E0003 di game.nrxl:5: variabel skor belum dibuat The code can be searched online even when the message is in another language.

Variables

be x = 5
be name = "Budi"
be x int = 5                 # with a type: int, float, double, bool,
                             # string, list, map
be active bool               # without a value: int/float/double = 0,
                             # bool = false, string = "",
                             # list = [], map = {}
be scores list int           # empty list of int
be ages map int              # empty map, values are int
be x += 1                    # also -=  *=  /=  %=
be items[0] = "a"            # set a list item
be ages["Budi"] = 21         # set a map value (new keys are created,
                             # starting at 0)
be p.hp -= 10                # set a type field / map value
be data.players[0].hp = 50   # nested
  • A variable must be created before it is read; otherwise it is an error.
  • Inside a function, new variables are local. Existing global variables can still be changed from inside a function.
  • for variables inside a function are always local: for i in a function does not change the main program's i.
  • Every be and for outside functions makes a global variable, including the ones inside a loop or if. If a function uses the same name with another kind, the error appears before the program runs, with the line number of that global:
loop running3d()
    be t = trim(typed)       # t is global, text
func shelf()
    be t = 0.5               # ERROR: t is already a global variable of type string

Strict types:

be x = 5                     # same as be x int = 5
be x = "hello"               # ERROR: x is an int
be x = 2.5                   # ERROR: decimal into int, use int(2.5)
be h = 2.5                   # no type: a decimal becomes double
be h float = 2.5             # float must be written out
be h = 3                     # allowed: int goes into double, becomes 3.0
  • A variable's kind is set when it is created (from the written type, or from its first value) and cannot change. The guess: 5 -> int, 2.5 / 5.0 -> double, "a" -> string, true -> bool.
  • List and map items must be one kind: [1, "two"] and add(scoreList, "x") are errors. [1, 2.5] is allowed and everything becomes double.
  • Mixed data (name and age together) uses a type, not a map.
  • be x = [] and be x = {} are errors because the item kind is unknown; write be x list int or be x map string.
  • Type fields keep the kind written in the type.
  • Decimals with a whole value print with .0 (4 / 2 -> 2.0) so they look different from ints.
  • fromJson results may be mixed, because JSON is mixed. Their type is json: be data json = fromJson(text). be data json alone = empty json {}. typeOf still names the shape of the content (map, list, ...).
  • be m[k] += value: if key k does not exist yet, it starts from the empty value of the map's item kind (0, 0.0, "", false). So be count[word] += 1 just works.
  • Function parameters follow the kind of the argument given.

Check before running: before the first line runs, nrxl checks the whole file (including the bodies of functions that are never called). If something is certainly wrong, the program does not run at all and the error shows right away:

be score = 10
be score += 0.5              # error before running: score is an int
add2(1, "two")               # error: parameter b is an int
func result() int
    return "text"            # error even if result() is never called
  • What is checked: values of variables whose kind is known, arguments and argument counts, return values, type fields, and lock variables.
  • Operators that are certainly wrong are checked too: "17" * 2, 10 == "10", list + 1.
  • Functions with untyped parameters are checked for every argument kind used: func minus(a, b) called as minus("five", 2) is an error right away.
  • If a value's kind is only known at run time (for example json content), that line is checked at run time as usual.
  • The body of a try block is not checked before running, because try exists to catch errors.

lock (a variable that cannot change):

lock PI = 3.14159
lock MAX_HP int = 100
lock COLORS = ["red", "blue"]
  • be PI = 3, be PI += 1, and for PI in ... are errors.
  • The content of a locked list/map is locked too: be COLORS[0] = ..., add(), takeLast(), and remove() are refused.
  • lock only creates new variables.

delete (remove a variable that is no longer used, like free() in C):

be data = [1, 2, 3]
delete data                  # its memory is released
delete a, b                  # several at once
  • After delete, reading that variable is an error like a variable that was never created. The name can be used again with be.
  • Inside a function, delete removes the local variable first, then the global one.
  • lock variables and variables owned by another file cannot be deleted.

Memory is cleaned up automatically (reference counting):

be a = [1, 2, 3]
be b = a                     # a and b hold the SAME list
add(b, 4)                    # a is now [1, 2, 3, 4] too
be a = [9]                   # b still holds the old list, so it is kept
  • Lists, maps, and type objects are freed as soon as no variable, list, or map holds them. delete is only needed to release memory sooner (for example big data in the middle of a program).
  • Text is always copied, so changing one text never changes another.
  • Do not put a list inside itself (add(a, a)): its memory is never freed.

Operators

+ - * / %            Arithmetic. % = remainder. Use ( ) for order.
                     / always gives a decimal: 7 / 2 -> 3.5,
                     4 / 2 -> 2.0. For a whole result: int(7 / 2) -> 3.
                     int with int stays int; if either side is a
                     decimal, the result is a decimal.
+                    Adds when both sides are numbers. Otherwise joins
                     text: "Age: " + 5 -> "Age: 5", "5" + 3 -> "53".
== != < > <= >=      Number with number, or text with text. The result is
                     true / false. Number with text is an error: 5 == "5".

Text holding a number (for example the result of ask) is still text. To calculate with it, convert it first: int("5") + 3 -> 8, float("2.5") * 2 -> 5.0, or use ask.int. "5" * 2, sqrt("16"), and -"5" are errors. and or not Logic. in not in Is inside a list / text / map keys: "orange" in fruits x[i] List item or character in text (index starts at 0). x["key"] x.field Map value or type field.

Joining without +: Text and values written side by side are joined directly, in print, be, and function arguments.

print "Hello " name "!"
be greeting = "Score: " score
writeFile("a.txt", "content " x)

A minus after text is read as subtraction, so wrap it in parentheses:

print "result " (-x)

Input and output

print "Hello " name
print                               # empty line
write("Loading", "...")             # like print, without a new line
write("\rLoading 50%")              # \r: back to the start, overwrite
be name = ask "Name? "
be age = ask.int "Age? "            # only accepts whole numbers
be age int = ask "Age? "            # same as ask.int
be x = ask "Hi " name ", age? "     # the prompt may contain variables
ask "Press Enter..."                # the input is thrown away
wait(1)                             # wait (seconds)
wait(0.5)                           # decimals are fine
wait.float(0.5)                     # same as wait(0.5)
wait.double(0.5)

Control flow

if / else if / else:

if x > 10
    print "big"
else if x > 5
    print "medium"
else
    print "small"

loop (while the condition is true):

be i = 0
loop i < 10
    print i
    be i += 1

for ... in:

for f in ["apple", "orange"]   # list items
for c in "abc"                 # each character
for k in people                # each map key
for i in range(5)              # 0, 1, 2, 3, 4

break / continue:

for i in range(10)
    if i == 2
        continue               # go to the next round
    if i == 5
        break                  # leave the loop
break and continue also work from inside if, try, and options.

options (pick one):

options choice
    option "1"
        print "Play"
    option "2", "3"            # several values at once
        print "Quit"
    else                       # optional
        print "None"
Only the first matching option runs. Matching works like ==
(option 4 matches "4").

try / catch / throw:

try
    be content = readFile("data.txt")
catch err                      # plain "catch" is fine too
    print "failed: " err
throw "error message"          # raise your own error
Every nrxl error (including ones from libraries and functions) can be
caught.

exit:

exit()                         # stop the program
exit(3)                        # with exit code 3

Functions

func area(w, h)
    return w * h
print area(4, 5)               # used in an expression
greet()                        # called as a statement

Default parameter values:

func greet(name, word = "Hello")
    return word ", " name
greet("Budi")                  # Hello, Budi
greet("Budi", "Hi")            # Hi, Budi
func times(a, b = a * 2)       # a default may use earlier parameters
  • Parameters without defaults must come first.
  • At most 8 parameters. A function may call itself (recursion).
  • return without a value returns empty text.

Parameter and result types (optional, recommended):

func add2(a int, b int) int
    return a + b
func circleArea(r double) double
    return 3.14 * r * r
func greet(name string, word string = "Hello") string
func heal(p Player, n int = 10) Player      # a type name is a type too
  • The type goes after the parameter name, the result type after the ).
  • Arguments that do not fit are an error right away: add2(1, "two"), add2(1, 2.5). An int may go into a double parameter.
  • If a result type is written, the function must return a matching value. return 7 / 2 in an int function is an error; use int(7 / 2).
  • Untyped parameters follow the kind of the argument given.

Type (new types, like classes)

type Player
    name string
    hp int = 100                       # defaults are fine
    level int = 1
init name, level                   # no parentheses, optional
    be own.name = name
    be own.level = level
func attack(n int)                 # method; own = this object
    be own.hp -= n
func info() string
    return own.name " hp=" own.hp
be p = Player("Budi", 3)               # calls init
p.attack(30)
print p.info()                         # Budi hp=70
print typeOf(p)                        # Player

Without init, values fill the fields in order:

type Point
    x int
    y int
be t = Point(1, 2)                     # number of values = number of fields
  • Every field must have a type; its kind cannot change.
  • own only exists inside init and methods.
  • A type name can also be a parameter type, result type, and list item type: be team list Player, func heal(p Player) Player.
  • At most 16 fields. A misspelled field or method is an error right away.
  • struct has been removed; use type.

Other files, export, libraries, and ffi

im (use your own .nrxl file):

im calc                        # = calc.nrxl
im "calc.nrxl"
im tools/calc                  # = tools/calc.nrxl
im "tools/calc"
  • nrxl looks for the file from the folder of the file that writes im.
  • The same file is only loaded once.
  • im must be written at the far left (not indented).
  • im is a reserved word: it cannot be a function or type name, and im() is always an error. A variable named im (be im = 5) is still allowed.

im ... from (take only certain names):

im area, Point from "tools"    # from tools.nrxl, only area and Point
im area from tools             # without quotes is fine too
  • Other names exported (ex) in tools.nrxl cannot be used from this file. The error says which name needs to be added to im.
  • Every name written must be exported in that file; otherwise it is an error before the program runs.
  • im "tools" without from is still allowed, and opens everything exported.

ex (export): In a file used through im, only what has ex can be used by other files.

ex func circleArea(r)
    return tidy(PI * r * r)
ex type Point
    x int
    y int
ex be NAME = "calc"
ex lock PI = 3.14159
func tidy(x)                   # no ex: only for this file
    return round(x, 2)
  • The main file (the one run directly) does not need ex.
  • The same name in different files does not clash as long as it is not exported.
  • ex must be written at the far left, outside functions.

lib (built-in libraries):

lib nrx_window.h
lib nrx_rand.h
lib nrx_crudfile.h
lib nrx_keyboard.h
lib nrx_console.h
lib nrx_sound.h
lib nrx_json.h
lib nrx_http.h
lib nrx_3d.h

Library features can only be used after their lib line.

ffi (call C / DLL functions directly):

ffi "user32.dll" (
    func MessageBoxA(hwnd int, text string, title string, kind int) int
    func SetCursorPos(x int, y int) int
)
ffi "kernel32.dll" (
    func GetTickCount() int
    func Sleep(ms int)                 # no result kind = returns
)                                      # nothing
MessageBoxA(0, "Hello from nrxl!", "Message", 0)
SetCursorPos(100, 200)
Argument and result kinds:
  int        32-bit whole number (also BOOL, UINT, DWORD in C)
  int64      64-bit whole number
  float      32-bit decimal
  double     64-bit decimal
  string     text (char* in C)
  pointer    address / handle (HWND, HANDLE, H..., *); 0 = NULL
  • Write "name kind" for each argument (the name may be left out, the kind is enough). The result kind goes after the closing parenthesis.
  • At most 12 arguments. Windows 64-bit only.
  • nrxl checks the DLL file and function name while reading the program, so a typo is an error before the program runs.
  • ffi functions win over built-in functions with the same name (e.g. sqrt).
  • An ffi function name cannot be the same as your own nrxl function/type.
  • ffi functions can be called from every file (no ex needed).
  • Another name for a DLL function: write "as RealName" after the result kind.
ffi "msvcrt.dll" (
    func length(s string) int as strlen
)

Buffers (raw memory for C structs, arrays, and output text):

newBuffer(n)                 n zero bytes, returns the address (pointer)
poke(p, offset, kind, value) write value at p + offset
peek(p, offset, kind)        read the value at p + offset
peekText(p)                  zero-terminated text at p (peekText(p, offset))
freeBuffer(p)                give the memory back
kind: "int8", "int16", "int", "int64", "float", "double", "pointer"
# C struct { int x; double y; } = 16 bytes (y starts at byte 8)
be s = newBuffer(16)
poke(s, 0, "int", 5)
poke(s, 8, "double", 2.5)
cFunction(s)                 # passed as a pointer
print peek(s, 8, "double")
freeBuffer(s)
  • A struct passed by value (not a pointer) that is 8 bytes or smaller: read it first with peek(s, 0, "int64"), then pass it as int64.
  • A wrong address crashes the program; nrxl cannot check it.

Callbacks (nrxl functions called by C code):

func compare(a int, b int) int
    return peek(a, 0, "int") - peek(b, 0, "int")
qsort(data, count, 4, callback("compare"))
  • callback("name") gives a pointer to that function. At most 16 functions, each with up to 4 whole-number/pointer parameters; the result is a whole number. Callbacks must be called on the same thread (like qsort, EnumWindows).

Built-in functions (no lib)

Function names are case-sensitive: getKey() is right, getkey() is wrong.

List

len(x)                   number of list items (also text length / number
                         of map keys)     len([1, 2]) -> 2
add(list, value)         add at the end of the list
                         add(fruits, "mango")
takeLast(list)           take out and return the last item
                         takeLast([1, 2, 3]) -> 3
remove(list, i)          take out the item at index i
                         remove(fruits, 0)
sort(list)               a new sorted list
                         sort([3, 1, 2]) -> [1, 2, 3]
filled(n, value)         a list of n copies of the same value, made at once
                         filled(3, 0) -> [0, 0, 0]
reverse(x)               reverse the order (also for text)
                         reverse([1, 2, 3]) -> [3, 2, 1]
indexOf(x, value)        first position, or -1 if not found
                         indexOf(["a", "b"], "b") -> 1
slice(x, start, end)     take from start up to before end
                         (end optional, negative = from the back)
                         slice([1, 2, 3, 4], 1, 3) -> [2, 3]
contains(x, value)       true / false (same as in)

Array (numbers only, fastest)

array(n)                 n numbers 0.0          array(3) -> [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
array(n, value)          n equal numbers        array(2, 7) -> [7.0, 7.0]
array(list)              number list to array   array([1, 2]) -> [1.0, 2.0]
be pos array = array(1000)
be pos[0] = 2.5
be pos[1] += 1
print pos[0] + pos[1]
  • Items are always decimals (double), like double[] in C: a[i] is a double, so use int(a[i]) for an int.
  • len, add, in, for x in a, lock, print, and toJson work like for lists.
  • Uses less memory than a list, and in a built .exe math with a[i] becomes a plain C double (can be several times faster than a list).
  • In ffi, an array can be passed to a pointer parameter as double*.

Map

keys(m)                  list of all keys
values(m)                list of all values
remove(m, key)           take out a key, return its value
contains(m, key)         whether the key exists
len(m)                   number of keys

Text

trim(t)                  remove spaces at the start and end
                         trim("  Budi  ") -> "Budi"
upper(t)  lower(t)       upper / lower case
                         upper("hello") -> "HELLO"
split(t)                 split on spaces
                         split("a  b") -> ["a", "b"]
split(t, separator)      split on a separator ("" = per character)
                         split("a,b", ",") -> ["a", "b"]
join(list, separator)    join list items (separator optional)
                         join(["a", "b"], "-") -> "a-b"
replace(t, find, with)   replace every match
                         replace("tea tea", "tea", "coffee") -> "coffee coffee"
contains(t, part)        contains("hello", "ell") -> true
indexOf(t, part)         indexOf("hello", "lo") -> 3
substr(t, start, length)
                         substr("Hello World", 0, 5) -> "Hello"
                         (length optional)
slice(t, start, end)     slice("nrxlang", -4) -> "lang"
reverse(t)               reverse("hello") -> "olleh"

Conversion

str(x)                   to text
int(x)                   to a whole number (error if not a number)
float(x)                 to a decimal
typeOf(x)                "int", "double", "string", "bool", "list", "map",
                         or the type name (float also shows "double")

Numbers and math

range(end)                     range(3) -> [0, 1, 2]
range(start, end)              range(2, 5) -> [2, 3, 4]
range(start, end, step)        range(10, 0, -3) -> [10, 7, 4, 1]
abs(x)                         abs(-5) -> 5
round(x)  round(x, digits)     round(2.567, 2) -> 2.57
floor(x)  ceil(x)              floor(2.9) -> 2
sqrt(x)                        sqrt(16) -> 4
sin(x), cos(x), tan(x)         angle in radians: sin(pi() / 2) -> 1
atan2(y, x)                    angle (radians) of point (x, y), -pi..pi
pi()                           3.14159...; degrees to radians: d * pi() / 180
pow(a, b)                      pow(2, 10) -> 1024
min(...)  max(...)             max(3, 9, 2) -> 9   max([3, 9, 2]) -> 9

Time and program

time()                   "HH:MM:SS"
date()                   "YYYY-MM-DD"
timer()                  seconds since the program started
exit()  exit(code)       stop the program

Libraries

lib nrx_window.h - windows, buttons, canvas

templateStyle (look):

templateStyle title(
    size: 28
    bold: true
    color: "blue"
)
Properties:
  size: 20                  font size (pixels)
  font: "Consolas"          font
  bold: true                bold
  italic: true              italic
  color: "blue"             text color
  background: "#1e1e2e"     background color
  width: 120                element width (automatic without it)
  height: 40                element height (automatic without it)
  hover: "#b4befe"          button background under the cursor
  hoverColor: "white"       button text under the cursor
  • Used by naming it: newText("Hello", 20, 20, title). One element can use at most 4 styles.
  • In newWindow: background = window background; size, font, bold, italic become the default for everything inside; color becomes the text default.
  • Order of precedence: window style -> element style -> size/color arguments.

windowTemplate (window content):

windowTemplate menu(
    newText(text, x, y, fontSize, color, style)
    newButton(onclick(function()), text, x, y, fontSize, style)
    newInput(variable, x, y, width, fontSize, style)
    newCheck(variable, "text", x, y, fontSize, style)
    newSelect(variable, choices, x, y, width, fontSize, style)
    newList(variable, choices, x, y, width, height, fontSize, style)
    newCanvas(name, x, y, width, height, style)
    newImage("file.png", x, y, width, height, style)
    onKey(function())
    onMouse(function())
    onTimer(function(), seconds)
)
  • Arguments after the x, y position may be left out. A style name may be placed anywhere at the end.
  • Text may contain variables ("Score: " score) and updates automatically.
  • newInput, newCheck, newSelect, newList are linked both ways with their variable. newCheck holds true/false; newSelect/newList hold the chosen text; choices is a list.
  • newCanvas(screen, ...) also creates the variable screen for the drawing functions.
  • At most 32 items per template.

Events:

onclick(f()) in newButton   f()                    button clicked
onKey(f())                  f(key)                 keyboard key pressed
onMouse(f())                f(x, y, action, canvas) mouse on a canvas
                                                   action: "left", "right",
                                                   "release", "move"
onTimer(f(), seconds)       f()                    called repeatedly every
                                                   few seconds (max. 4)
  • The function may take fewer parameters than are sent, for example func click(x, y).
  • In a window with onKey, keyboard keys only go to onKey (except Tab, and while typing in a newInput).

Opening and closing windows:

newWindow("Title", width, height)
newWindow("Title", width, height, menu)          # with a template
newWindow("Title", width, height, menu, dark)    # template and style
closeWindow("Title")                             # close one window
closeWindow()                                    # close all
  • Events run while the script is waiting (wait), or after the script ends.
  • The program only exits after every window is closed.

Drawing on a canvas:

clearCanvas(screen)                               # or with a color
clearCanvas(screen, "#1e1e2e")
drawRect(screen, x, y, width, height, color)
drawCircle(screen, x, y, radius, color)           # x, y = center
drawLine(screen, x1, y1, x2, y2, color, thick)    # thick optional
drawText(screen, text, x, y, color, fontSize)     # size optional (16)
drawImage(screen, "file.png", x, y)               # or + width, height
drawImage and newImage can open PNG, JPG, and BMP. Drawings appear on
screen at the end of every event or wait.

Window colors: black, white, red, green, blue, yellow, orange, purple, gray (or the Indonesian names hitam, putih, merah, hijau, biru, kuning, oranye, ungu, abu), or "#RRGGBB".

lib nrx_rand.h - random numbers

random()              random decimal from 0 up to below 1
random(min, max)      random whole number min..max
choice(list)          one random list item
randomSeed(n)         set the seed so the random sequence can repeat

lib nrx_crudfile.h - files

createFile(path)          create an empty file; false if it already exists
readFile(path)            the whole file as text
readLines(path)           the file as a list, one line per item
writeFile(path, text)     overwrite the file
writeLines(path, list)    overwrite the file, one list item per line
appendFile(path, text)    add text at the end of the file
appendLine(path, text)    add text as a new line
deleteFile(path)          delete the file; false if it fails
fileExists(path)          true if the file exists
listFiles(folder)         list of file and folder names (folders end in /)
readRange(path, start, n) list of n lines from line start (first line is 1)
findInFile(path, text)    list of line numbers that contain text
replaceInFile(path, old, new)  replace all, returns how many were replaced;
                          the file's line endings (CRLF/LF) are kept

lib nrx_keyboard.h - keyboard in the console

keyPressed("left")    true/false without waiting: key pressed since the
                      last check
getKey()              wait for one key, return its name

Key names: "a" to "z", "0" to "9", "left", "right", "up", "down", "space", "enter", "escape" or "esc", "tab", "backspace", "delete", "shift", "ctrl", "alt", "home", "end", "pageup", "pagedown", "f1" to "f12". onKey in windows uses the same names.

lib nrx_console.h - console display

clear()                   clear the screen
cursor(x, y)              move the cursor to column x, row y (from 0)
color("red")              text color for the next prints
color("white", "blue")    text + background color
color()                   back to the normal color
runCommand(command)       run a cmd command, returns its output (stdout and
                          stderr) as text: runCommand("dir")
commandStatus()           exit code of the last command (0 = success)

Console colors: black, red, green, yellow, blue, purple, cyan, white, gray (or the Indonesian names), or "#RRGGBB".

lib nrx_sound.h - sound

playSound("coin.wav")     play an effect once (several can overlap)
playMusic("song.mp3")     play music on repeat (replaces the old one)
stopMusic()               stop the music
stopSound()               stop all effects
Formats: WAV and MP3.

lib nrx_json.h - JSON

toJson(data)          nrxl data -> one-line JSON text
toJson(data, true)    same, but pretty (lines and indentation)
fromJson(text)        JSON text -> nrxl data
  • JSON object <-> map, array <-> list, true/false <-> bool, null -> empty text. Types are saved as objects.
  • To save and load data from a file, pair it with nrx_crudfile:
writeFile("data.json", toJson(data, true))
be result json = fromJson(readFile("data.json"))   # content may be mixed

lib nrx_http.h - internet (HTTP and HTTPS)

httpGet(url)                  page/data content as text
httpPost(url, body)           send text, returns the reply text
httpPost(url, body, kind)     with a content type, e.g. "application/json"
httpPost(url, body, kind, headers)  extra headers as a map of text
httpGet(url, headers)         same, for GET
httpStatus()                  status code of the last request (200, 404, ...)
lib nrx_http.h
lib nrx_json.h
be data json = fromJson(httpGet("https://api.example.com/data"))
if httpStatus() != 200
    print "failed: " httpStatus()
be headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + key}
be reply = httpPost(url, bodyJson, "application/json", headers)
  • A status other than 2xx is not an error; check it with httpStatus(). Only failing to connect (wrong address, no internet) is an error.

In the background (the program keeps running while it waits, e.g. a game window):

httpStart(url, body, kind, headers)  start sending, returns right away
httpDone()                    true when finished (or nothing is running)
httpResult()                  the reply; the status is in httpStatus()
httpPartial()                 text that arrived since the last httpPartial
                              (for streamed replies, e.g. "stream": true in
                              AI APIs); httpResult still holds the whole reply
httpStart(url, bodyJson, "application/json", headers)
loop running3d()
    if httpDone()
        be reply = httpResult()
    ...draw as usual...
  • One request at a time: the next httpStart is only allowed after httpResult. Connection errors appear at httpResult.

lib nrx_3d.h - simple 3D games (raylib)

open3d(title, width, height)          open a 3D window
running3d()                           true while the window is open
camera3d(x, y, z, lookX, lookY, lookZ)  camera and the point it looks at
begin3d(color)  ...  end3d()          one frame: background, draw, show
begin3d(top, bottom)                  gradient background from top to bottom
cube(x, y, z, width, height, depth, color)  box (sides shaded automatically
                                      so the shape is visible); cubeWire(...)
                                      only the edges
cylinder(x, y, z, topRadius, bottomRadius, height, color)
                                      cylinder; top radius 0 = cone;
                                      y = base of the cylinder
sphere(x, y, z, radius, color)        sphere
plane(x, y, z, width, depth, color)   flat floor
grid(count, spacing)                  helper lines on the floor
text2d(text, x, y, size, color)       text on screen (pixels)
rect2d(x, y, width, height, color)    rectangle on screen (pixels)
rectGrad2d(x, y, width, height, top, bottom)   2D gradient rectangle
textWidth2d(text, size)               text width in pixels
key3d("w")                            true while the key is held (letters,
                                      digits, space, enter, escape, shift,
                                      up, down, left, right, backspace,
                                      tab, ctrl)
pressed3d("enter")                    true once when pressed, repeating
                                      while held (for typing)
typed3d()                             characters typed since the last frame
clipboard3d()                         clipboard text (for Ctrl+V)
clipboard3d(text)                     put text on the clipboard (for copy)
screenshot3d("screen.png")            save the window content to .png
mouse3d()                             mouse position [x, y] in pixels
click3d()                             true once on a left click
wheel3d()                             mouse wheel movement this frame (+ up)
ground3d()                            floor point (y = 0) under the mouse:
                                      [x, z], or [] when pointing at the sky
toScreen3d(x, y, z)                   pixel position [x, y] of a 3D point,
                                      for labels above objects
exitKey3d("")                         key that closes the window (default
                                      escape; "" = only the X button)
fps3d(n)                              frames per second limit (default 60)
frameTime()                           seconds since the previous frame
close3d()                             close the window
colors: "red", "green", "blue", "white", "black", "gray", "darkgray",
        "yellow", "orange", "purple", "pink", "brown", "skyblue", "#rrggbb",
        "#rrggbbaa" (aa = transparency, 00 invisible to ff solid)
lib nrx_3d.h
open3d("Game", 800, 600)
be x = 0.0
loop running3d()
    if key3d("d")
        be x += 3 * frameTime()
    begin3d("skyblue")
    grid(10, 1)
    cube(x, 0.5, 0, 1, 1, 1, "orange")
    text2d("WASD", 10, 10, 20, "black")
    end3d()
close3d()

Rotating and moving (like transforms in other 3D programs):

push3d()                    # save the current position and direction
move3d(x, 0, z)             # everything drawn next moves to this point
turn3d("y", heading)        # then rotates (degrees) on axis "x", "y", "z"
cube(0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0.5, "orange")   # coordinates are now relative to it
push3d()                    # may nest (at most 16), e.g. an arm:
move3d(0.6, 1.8, 0)         #   move to the shoulder
turn3d("x", swing)          #   swing from the shoulder
cube(0, -0.4, 0, 0.3, 0.8, 0.3, "orange")
pop3d()
pop3d()                     # back to how it was before push3d
  • Every push3d must be closed with pop3d before end3d. text2d/rect2d only outside push3d.
  • Draw only between begin3d and end3d (screenshot3d after end3d).
  • The environment variable NRX3D_HIDDEN=1 keeps the window hidden (for automated tests); drawing and screenshot3d still work.
  • Full example with a text box: agen/kantor.nrxl.
  • A built .exe of a 3D program is about 1.7 MB (raylib is inside it); other programs do not carry raylib.

Limits

  • One line is at most 511 characters.
  • One program (including files pulled in with im) is at most 4096 lines.
  • At most 128 functions, 64 types, 1024 global variables, and 64 local variables per function.
  • lock inside a loop outside functions is an error on the second round (the variable already exists).

VS Code extension

The vscode-nrxl folder holds the extension for syntax colors and code snippets. How to install it, and later how to publish it, is in vscode-nrxl/README.md.
